SECRUKSince 2019

SECR

Streamlined Energy & Carbon Reporting

Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting requires large and quoted UK companies to publish their energy use and emissions in their annual report. There's no separate filing or deadline. It's due when your accounts are due.

Get SECR alerts

No fixed date

SECR disclosure in your annual report

Draft guide. We're checking this page against official sources before launch. Always confirm with your regulator.

Step 1

Are you in scope?

You're probably in if…

  • Quoted companies: global scope 1 and 2 emissions, an intensity ratio and energy-efficiency actions
  • Large unquoted companies and LLPs meeting two of: more than 250 employees, turnover over £36 million, balance sheet over £18 million

You're probably out if…

  • Companies using 40 MWh or less of energy in the UK in the year (they state this instead)
  • Small and medium-sized companies

Who regulates it: Companies House (filed with your accounts). The Financial Reporting Council oversees quality for larger companies.

Step 2

Your yearly routine

  1. Financial yearCollect energy and fuel data (gas, electricity, transport)
  2. Year endCalculate emissions using the government conversion factors
  3. With your accountsPublish in the directors' report. Private companies: 9 months after year end; public companies: 6 months
Step 3

Upcoming SECR deadlines 0

No fixed-date deadlines. See below.

Key facts

What to report
UK energy use, related emissions, at least one intensity ratio, efficiency actions
Thresholds
SECR kept its original £36m / £18m thresholds. The April 2025 Companies Act increases didn't change them
Coming
UK Sustainability Reporting Standards may replace or extend SECR
Overlap
Data can feed ESOS audits
Practical tip

Use the same conversion-factor year as your reporting year, and say so. It's the most common thing auditors query.

Recent changes

No changes logged for SECR yet. When a date or rule moves, it will appear here and in the monthly email.
